## Hook

Look up on a clear afternoon and the sky is blue. {c1} But sunlight is white. [beat] So where does the blue come from?

## Roadmap

In the next minute, one idea explains it, and the same idea explains red sunsets.

## 1: Scattered light

Here is the question to hold on to. Why blue, and not violet? Have a guess. [think]

Air molecules scatter short wavelengths far more than long ones. {c2} Blue light bounces around the whole sky, so blue reaches your eye from every direction. {c2,c3}

Violet scatters even more, but sunlight carries less of it, and our eyes are less sensitive to it. {c3} So the answer to the question is our eyes, as much as the air.

## Recap

Short wavelengths scatter most. [beat] At sunset, light crosses about forty times more air, the blue is scattered away, and red is left. {c4}

## Sign-off

That's the sky, plainly put. Thanks for listening.
